projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The network consistently reports 20-23 connected mobile devices from 05:40 to 06:57 with no camera activity or presence drop-off, indicating the household remains fully indoors with unusually high network activity for a Saturday morning. This likely reflects normal multi-device family routines, but a quick verification is recommended to rule out unexpected guests or unauthorized connections.

The stable 21–24 device count combined with zero motion, audio, or camera activity confirms a normal deep-sleep state, indicating the high presence count is background network activity from sleeping electronics rather than active users or guests.

The sustained 21–24 connected mobile devices with zero camera or audio activity at 2 AM strongly suggests a sleepover or late-night gaming session, with devices cycling through sleep modes. This is typical weekend behavior, but worth confirming if guests are expected.

The sustained 21–24 device connections paired with zero human or pet activity at nearly midnight on a Friday strongly indicates the house is unoccupied or in a deep rest state, with the high device count likely driven by IoT equipment, guest devices, or network artifacts rather than active occupants.

The sustained connection of 20–23 devices combined with zero motion, audio, camera, or pet activity for four hours strongly suggests the house is unoccupied or all electronics are idle while empty, which is highly unusual for a family with children and dogs during a Friday evening.

The sustained 19–22 connected devices paired with zero motion, audio, camera, or pet activity for four hours indicates the house is likely empty or all devices are in sleep/airplane mode, rather than a typical family evening. This stale presence data should be verified to rule out network reporting errors or ensure no one is inadvertently locked inside.

The consistent 19–21 device count combined with zero motion, audio, camera, or pet activity for four hours strongly indicates the house is unoccupied, with all devices left charging or stationary, rather than the family being home and inactive.

The consistent 19–22 device count paired with zero motion, audio, or camera activity for four hours strongly indicates the household is gathered in a single sensor-dead zone (e.g., media room or closed living area) or all devices are stationary/charging together. This points to a prolonged quiet gathering like a movie night or gaming session, but warrants a quick check-in to rule out sensor failure or ensure well-being.

The persistent presence of 20+ mobile devices combined with zero physical activity (camera, motion, audio) for over four hours strongly suggests the house is either unoccupied with devices left running, or the occupants are in a prolonged inactive state, warranting a quick safety check-in.

The persistent 18–21 device count paired with zero motion, audio, or camera activity for four hours on a Friday afternoon strongly suggests the presence system is misclassifying smart home infrastructure (routers, hubs, or IoT devices) as mobile devices, or that all occupants are away with devices left on auto-connect. A quick network audit or check-in call would clarify whether this is a configuration artifact or an unreported absence.
